newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African Spoornet restructures to aim for market.
newsitem.headline: S.African Spoornet restructures to aim for market.

text.p: Spoornet, the rail subsidiary of South Africa's Transnet transport parastatal, said on Friday that it is rejigging its management structure as part of a three-year drive to diversify and become more market-driven.
The firm aims to shift from just shipping freight by rail and move into road transportation and warehousing.
"We want to move away from being just a rail firm to be a logistics solutions provider in which rail is only a part," a Spoornet spokesman told Reuters.
"Spoornet has reached a point now where we have to change to go into the future," he added.
Spoornet chief executive Braam le Roux said in a statement that the group's profitability was under pressure in its current freight shipping operations.
"Despite many profitable activities in our portfolio of services our operating profit is coming under increasing pressure to cover finance and other charges," he said.
The firm is to seek to become more market-driven and commercialised, but will stop short of full privatisation. Instead it is on the hunt for potential private sector partners.
"Partnerships, joint-ventures and alliances are seen as a possible way to obtain the necessary competitivenes," le Roux said.
He added that the firm did not intend to acquire additional substantial freight facilties.
The details of the restructuring include:
- Scrapping the current structure of 10 regional managers.
- Replacing the existing six business segments with 20 based classified by industry type. These segments will be further sub-divided to focus on customers.
- Centralisation of marketing by moving regional marketing staff to headquarters and creating a strategic marketing department.
- Spoornet's coal and iron ore export operations will be developed into self-contained business units.
- The creation of an innovative operation to seek out international business opportunities suitable for joint-ventures.
Le Roux said the moves would tackle Spoornet's biggest current shortcoming of not having a proper focus on the market.
The spokesman said there would be no job losses involved in the restructuring.
